rule: On-screen technical text may only restate these verified claims. Anything else is a new claim: verify it against the pinned corpus first, or leave it off screen.
verdicts: verified = anchored to the pinned RFC text; opinion = framing with no factual claim

lines.speaker: ADA
lines.text: How did web pages get live updates before WebSockets?

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: By polling, which the WebSocket R-F-C calls an abuse of H-T-T-P.

claims.claim: Before WebSockets, bidirectional web apps polled the server for updates; RFC 6455 calls this an abuse of HTTP.

anchors.snippet: has required an abuse of HTTP to poll the server for updates

claims.claim: RFC 6455 is the WebSocket Protocol RFC.

anchors.snippet: The WebSocket Protocol

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: R-F-C sixty-four-fifty-five offers one T-C-P connection instead, carrying traffic in both directions.

anchors.snippet: Request for Comments: 6455

claims.claim: The WebSocket Protocol provides a single TCP connection for traffic in both directions.

anchors.snippet: A simpler solution would be to use a single TCP connection for traffic in both directions.
This is what the WebSocket Protocol provides.

claims.claim: It is offered as an alternative to HTTP polling ('instead').

anchors.snippet: it provides an alternative to HTTP polling for two-way communication

lines.speaker: ADA
lines.text: So how does a WebSocket connection start?

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: As an ordinary H-T-T-P request that asks to upgrade: Upgrade websocket, Connection Upgrade.

claims.claim: The client's opening handshake is an HTTP Upgrade request; to an HTTP server it looks like a regular GET request with an Upgrade offer.

anchors.snippet: the WebSocket client's handshake is an HTTP Upgrade request
be a regular GET request with an Upgrade offer

claims.claim: It carries an Upgrade header containing websocket and a Connection header containing Upgrade.

anchors.snippet: The request MUST contain an |Upgrade| header field whose value MUST include the "websocket" keyword.
The request MUST contain a |Connection| header field whose value MUST include the "Upgrade" token.
Upgrade: websocket Connection: Upgrade

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: It adds a random key, and asks for protocol version thirteen.

claims.claim: The request carries Sec-WebSocket-Key, a randomly selected nonce.

anchors.snippet: nonce consisting of a randomly selected 16-byte value that has been base64-encoded
The nonce MUST be selected randomly for each connection.
The value of this header field MUST be 13.
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: If it accepts, it answers one-oh-one, Switching Protocols, with an accept header.

claims.claim: A server that accepts the connection replies with status 101 (HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols).

anchors.snippet: If the server chooses to accept the incoming connection, it MUST reply with a valid HTTP response indicating the following.
A Status-Line with a 101 response code as per RFC 2616
HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols

claims.claim: The reply includes a Sec-WebSocket-Accept header field.

anchors.snippet: A |Sec-WebSocket-Accept| header field.
Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: Any other status code, and H-T-T-P semantics still apply.

claims.claim: Any status code other than 101 means the handshake has not completed and HTTP semantics still apply.

anchors.snippet: Any status code other than 101 indicates that the WebSocket handshake has not completed and that the semantics of HTTP still apply.

lines.speaker: MAX
lines.text: Then frames flow both ways, whenever either side wants.

claims.claim: After a successful handshake the data transfer starts: a two-way channel where each side sends data at will.

anchors.snippet: Once the client and server have both sent their handshakes, and if the handshake was successful, then the data transfer part starts.
This is a two-way communication channel where each side can, independently from the other, send data at will.

claims.claim: Data is transmitted as a sequence of frames.

anchors.snippet: In the WebSocket Protocol, data is transmitted using a sequence of frames.
